reason: E1 and E2 show that Al+Ti additions form coherent γ′ precipitates in Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti systems, supporting the first two premises. However, none of the cited evidence directly demonstrates that increasing Al alone (with reduced Cr) in a Ti-Ni-primary HEA enhances high-temperature strength while preserving ductility, nor does it validate the specific aging treatment of 800 °C for 1 hour. E3 discusses ductile, coherent precipitates but in a different alloy system, and E4 is cited as conflicting but actually describes Ti-induced heterogeneity, not Al effects.
premises: Al addition to FCC HEAs promotes γ′ precipitate formation
γ′ precipitates are coherent with the FCC matrix
Coherent γ′ precipitates increase high-temperature yield strength
Ductility is preserved with coherent γ′ precipitates
Aging at ~800 °C for 1 hour produces the desired precipitate distribution
